data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: academic
sections.summary: Relating to education and study at a school, college or university; or a person who teaches and does research at a university.

senses.definition: relating to education and scholarship, especially at college or university level
examples: Her academic achievements earned her a place at a top university.

senses.definition: a person who teaches or does research at a university or college
examples: Leading academics from around the world attended the international conference.

answers.answer: Her academic record impressed the university admissions committee.
She submitted her academic to the professor two days before the deadline.
He was excited to collect his academic from the office after the ceremony.
The academic weather that morning made it impossible to hold the outdoor event.

sections.question: curriculum
sections.summary: The subjects or courses of study offered by a school or university, or the content covered in a particular course.

senses.definition: the subjects that are included in a course of study or taught in a school, college or university
examples: The school revised its curriculum to include digital literacy as a core subject.

senses.definition: all the courses of study offered by an educational institution
examples: The national curriculum sets out what children should learn at each stage of their education.

answers.answer: The school introduced coding into its curriculum from the age of seven.
She prepared her curriculum carefully before applying for the teaching position.
He forgot to bring his curriculum to class, so he could not follow the lesson.
The student read the curriculum from cover to cover the night before the exam.

sections.question: diploma
sections.summary: An official document or certificate awarded by a school, college or university to show that you have successfully completed a course of study.

senses.definition: a document given by a college or university to show that you have passed an examination or completed a course of study
examples: After three years of study, she received her diploma in graphic design.

senses.definition: a course of study at a college or university that is shorter than a degree
examples: He enrolled in a one-year diploma in business management.

answers.answer: She proudly displayed her diploma on the wall of her new office.
He wrote a formal diploma to thank the school for the excellent teaching he received.
The two governments signed a diploma to improve trade relations between their countries.
She diploma the class every week with a short written test.

sections.question: elective
sections.summary: A course or subject that a student can choose to study, rather than one that is required; also used as an adjective to describe something that is optional or chosen freely.

senses.definition: a course that a student can choose to take rather than one that is compulsory
examples: She chose photography as her elective for the spring semester.

senses.definition: not compulsory; chosen freely by a student or patient
examples: Elective modules allow students to explore subjects beyond their core degree.

answers.answer: As part of her degree, she could take one elective from a list of twelve subjects.
The students had an elective vote at the end of the school year to choose a class president.
He was a very elective student who always chose the most efficient way to study.
The teacher told the class to be elective when deciding which questions to answer first.

sections.question: enrollment
sections.summary: The process of officially registering or signing up for a course, school or programme; also refers to the total number of students registered.

senses.definition: the act of officially registering to take part in a course or programme
examples: Online enrollment for the spring semester opens on the first of December.

senses.definition: the total number of students registered at a school or university
examples: The university reported a record enrollment of over 30,000 students this year.

answers.answer: Enrollment for next year's programme closes at the end of this month.
The teacher took enrollment at the start of every class to see who was present.
Her enrollment in the final exam was 92 out of 100, the highest in the class.
He sent his enrollment to three different universities hoping for an offer.

sections.question: faculty
sections.summary: The teaching staff of a university or college; also a division of a university specialising in a particular subject area; also a natural ability or power.

senses.definition: a group of related university departments forming a larger division of the university
examples: She applied to the Faculty of Engineering and was offered a place on the mechanical engineering course.

senses.definition: the teaching and research staff of a university or college
examples: The faculty voted to revise the assessment criteria for all undergraduate courses.

senses.definition: a natural ability or power of the mind or body
examples: Even at the age of ninety, she retained all her mental faculties.

answers.answer: He graduated from the Faculty of Law after completing four years of study.
She packed her faculty into her bag every morning before leaving for class.
The students read through the entire faculty before writing their essays.
He was a very faculty person who always knew the answer to every question.

sections.question: lecture
sections.summary: A talk given to a group of students or an audience on a particular subject, especially at a university; also used as a verb meaning to give such a talk.

senses.definition: a formal talk given to a group of students or an audience, especially at a university
examples: The professor's lecture on the causes of the First World War lasted ninety minutes.

senses.definition: to give a formal talk to a class or large group, especially at a university
examples: She lectures on contemporary literature at the University of Edinburgh.

answers.answer: The biology lecture covered three important topics related to cell division.
She studied her lecture carefully the evening before the exam.
The students handed in their lecture at the end of the class.
He wrote a lecture to explain to the teacher why he had missed the previous session.

sections.question: prerequisite
sections.summary: Something that must exist or happen before something else is possible; a course or qualification that must be completed before you can take a more advanced course.

senses.definition: something that must be done or achieved before something else can happen or be done
examples: A good knowledge of statistics is a prerequisite for the data analysis module.

senses.definition: required as a prior condition before something else can take place
examples: Students must complete the prerequisite modules before joining the advanced seminar.

answers.answer: Calculus is listed as a prerequisite for the advanced physics course.
The teacher gave the class a prerequisite to complete and hand in by Friday.
She submitted her prerequisite report two days before the end of term.
He read the prerequisite quickly and highlighted the most important passages.

sections.question: scholarship
sections.summary: Money given to a student by an institution to help pay for their education, usually based on academic achievement or financial need; also refers to serious academic study and research.

senses.definition: an amount of money given to a student to help pay for their education, usually because of academic achievement or financial need
examples: She was awarded a full scholarship to study medicine at Cambridge University.

senses.definition: serious academic study and the knowledge gained from it
examples: His scholarship in the field of medieval history is internationally recognised.

answers.answer: He won a scholarship that covered his full tuition fees for three years.
The teacher gave a scholarship to every student who completed the homework on time.
She left her scholarship on the desk and the teacher collected it at the end of class.
He scholarship in English for two years before sitting his final university exams.

sections.question: thesis
sections.summary: A long piece of writing based on original research, submitted as part of a university degree, especially a postgraduate degree; also refers to a statement or theory put forward to be proved or discussed.

senses.definition: a long piece of original research written as part of a university degree, especially a master's or doctoral degree
examples: She spent two years researching and writing her doctoral thesis on climate migration.

senses.definition: a statement or idea that is discussed and argued about in a formal way
examples: The central thesis of his book is that language shapes how we think.

answers.answer: He submitted his master's thesis after three years of research and writing.
The teacher asked the class to write a short thesis about what they did at the weekend.
She handed in her thesis to the teacher at the end of the lesson for marking.
The students read through the thesis quickly the night before the test.
